entries.reason: Generated by the :awake:core:text:generateGraphemeBreakTable task (GenerateGraphemeBreakTableTask in build-logic) from GraphemeBreakProperty.txt, emoji/emoji-data.txt and DerivedCoreProperties.txt: the grapheme break properties are Unicode data, not code, and no Kotlin Multiplatform library covering every Core target ships them.
Unicode's own conformance cases for UAX #29 grapheme clusters, copied unchanged so GraphemeBreakConformanceTest checks the iterator against them.

The official prebuilt Basis Universal transcoder's Emscripten loader, copied unchanged, so the browser can transcode KTX2 textures to the GPU's block format (#1211). BinomialLLC publishes no npm package, and the small Khronos transcoders handle UASTC only, not ETC1S. Its SHA-256 is checked at build time by the verifyBasisTranscoder task, which fails the build on a mismatch.

BinomialLLC publishes no npm package, and the small Khronos transcoders handle UASTC only, not ETC1S. Khronos' PBR Neutral tone curve, adapted from the reference GLSL into the post-processing stack's tone-mapping stage (ASL). The reference file carries no header of its own, so the repository's LICENSE.md, Apache-2.0, covers it; the folder's README.md, which describes the curve, is marked CC-BY-4.0. Both are satisfied by keeping Khronos' copyright on the snippet and attributing Khronos in NOTICE.md. Adapted, not depended on: the curve is a few lines that must run inside Awake's own shader DSL, and Khronos publishes no library to call.

Khronos' PBR Neutral tone curve, adapted from the reference GLSL into the CPU twin the stack's tests compare that stage against. The reference file carries no header of its own, so the repository's LICENSE.md, Apache-2.0, covers it; the folder's README.md, which describes the curve, is marked CC-BY-4.0. Both are satisfied by keeping Khronos' copyright on the snippet and attributing Khronos in NOTICE.md. Adapted, not depended on: the curve is a few lines that must run inside Awake's own shader DSL, and its CPU twin must match the shader step for step, and Khronos publishes no library to call.

FxaaShader, the post-processing stack's FXAA-style edge anti-aliasing (simplified: luma contrast test, edge orientation, subpixel blend; no end-of-edge search). Added in #970 with no recorded source, and the owner can't trace one (#1791). Its structure differs from NVIDIA's FXAA 3.11: it has no end-of-edge search and a different subpixel term. Its tuning constants (the 0.0833 minimum contrast and the 0.25, 0.166 and 0.125 relative thresholds) are the published FXAA values. It is not certified clean-room. It stays, labelled as what it is, because a second from-memory implementation would have no better provenance; it is to be replaced if a verifiably licensed FXAA or SMAA source is adopted (#1791).

AMD FidelityFX CAS (Contrast Adaptive Sharpening, non-scaling 5-tap sharpen and 12-tap edge-thinning upscale+sharpen, green-channel weight mode), adapted from ffx_cas.h into Awake's shader DSL (ASL) for the single-pass scene scale-up shader (#1830). Selected over three surveyed vendor alternatives: AMD FidelityFX FSR 1.0 (GPUOpen-Effects/FidelityFX-FSR commit a21ffb8f6c13233ba336352bdff293894c706575, MIT, two full-screen passes EASU+RCAS requiring an extra full-res target), NVIDIA Image Scaling (NVIDIAGameWorks/NVIDIAImageScaling commit 35e13ba316c98eeecf16f37eae70ce88019911f6, MIT, compute-shader + LUT architecture incompatible with Awake's fragment ImagePassChain), and Snapdragon Game Super Resolution (SnapdragonGameStudios/snapdragon-gsr commit d926f074bcb9d714e179f1ce0fcb9ee2eeb5074e, BSD-3-Clause-Clear). Adapted rather than depended on because the filter runs inside Awake's own ASL fragment pass shared by Vulkan and WebGPU, and upstream ships HLSL/GLSL headers only.
